title: Create a GitHub Repo
intro: A step-by-step path to create a GitHub account, make a repository, and get your website files onto GitHub.

steps.title: What a repository is
body: A repository (repo) is a project folder that GitHub stores for you, including a history of changes.
Think of it as both storage and a timeline: every commit is a snapshot with a short message explaining what changed.

images.caption: You can see all the files the last commit that altered the files and the readme.

tips: You do not need to master Git before creating your first repo.

steps.title: Create a GitHub account
body: Go to github.com and sign up. Choose a username carefully — it appears in default site URLs (username.github.io).
Verify your email so you can create repositories. Enable two-factor authentication when you can.
It is very important to use a home email, so that you can recieve any emails from gihub and so that you can keep your github acount after you graduate.
mistakes: Using an email you cannot access for verification.

steps.title: Create a repository
body: Click the + or new → New repository. Choose a name (for example my-website). What every you choose tthe website will be username.github.io/your-repository-name
Public repositories can use free GitHub Pages later. Add a README if you want a starting file. You can skip .gitignore and license while learning. Then create the repository.
tips: For a user site, a special repo named USERNAME.github.io publishes at the root domain.
For project sites, any repo name works and the URL includes the repo name.
mistakes: Making the repo private when you expected free Pages (private Pages needs a paid plan).

steps.title: Create your website files
body: A simple site needs at least index.html. Addding a style.css and script.js is good practice but not necessary, the same thing can be done with <style> and <script> elements. You can also add them later
You can write files in any text IDE (VS Code is recommended) or create them on GitHub later.

images.caption: This is without having a style.css or script.js file.
This is with a style.css and script.js file.

tips: Start with one index.html file if you want the shortest path.

steps.title: Committing files to the repository
body: On vs code go to the source contorl tab → type in the commit message → click the commit button and then click the sync button.
Or on GitHub: open the repo → Add file → Upload files → drag your files → type a commit message → commit, this is the same as the vs code method.

links.label: After committing files: Publish with GitHub Pages

tips: Commit messages should say why you changed something, e.g. “Add homepage markup”. this is for your own reference and so that others can understand your changes. Also without a commit message you will not be able to push your changes to the repository.
